If I could change the world in just one way, I’d instill true empathy and understanding at scale—so that every person, from every background, could genuinely see and feel what it’s like to walk in someone else’s shoes. 

Why empathy?

• It breaks down barriers of race, nationality, faith, gender, age and ideology, replacing fear and suspicion with curiosity and respect.  
• It inspires more compassionate policies—on healthcare, education, justice and the environment—because decision-makers would personally grasp the real-world impacts of their choices.  
• It powers cooperation rather than competition, so communities work together to solve problems instead of fighting over scarce resources.  
• It enhances mental health and social cohesion, as people feel heard, valued and connected rather than isolated or dehumanized.  

In practice, cultivating empathy would mean:

1. Education that teaches perspective-taking and active listening from an early age.  
2. Media and technology designed not merely to entertain or monetize attention, but to build bridges of understanding—showcasing diverse human experiences.  
3. Public spaces and civic initiatives that foster genuine, sustained interaction among different groups.  

With deeper empathy woven into our cultures and institutions, many of the world’s toughest challenges—conflict, inequality, environmental collapse—become far easier to address, because we’d actually care about one another’s well-being rather than treating people as abstractions or “others.” That single shift in collective mindset could transform everything else.
